test.title: Murray 4: two seas crossing (moguls)
test.purpose: Two wind seas 35 degrees apart make short peaks: here there is something to choose between within 30 degrees, so aiming at the dark faces should matter most. Murray Stewart's cues (Rottnest camp, November 2026): catch a wave, as square as needed; stay high on its face (ease off, let the push hold you); scan 3 to 8 m ahead of the bow, within 30 degrees either side, for darker patches on the back faces ahead; when one is in reach, sprint to drop and move to it, to be on the upper part of the next wave's face there; prefer running diagonal to square.
lookFor: the peaks where the two seas add up: are their back faces the darkest patches?
how far the best peak is off the heading
